HardwareBoardLabelFile.description:
Board-silkscreen label discovered or recorded during board mapping.

Labels are metadata for humans and tooling. They do not create claimable
resources by themselves; resources come from [`HardwareResourceFile`].

HardwareBoardLabelStatus.description: Verification status for a board label in a manifest file.

HardwareResourceFile.description:
Serializable resource entry in a board manifest file.

GPIO resources are often grouped under `gpio` in TOML for readability, while
non-GPIO resources live under `resource`; both convert to [`HwResource`].

HardwareTarget.description: Build or runtime target that a board manifest describes.

HwCapability.description:
Capability advertised by a [`crate::HwResource`].

Drivers check capabilities before claiming resources. A single resource may
expose multiple capabilities, such as a GPIO that can be used for input or
output.

oneOf.description: GPIO can drive an output level or waveform.
GPIO can be sampled as an input.
Timing resource can drive WS281x-class LED protocols.

HwMeasuredLimit.description:
One measured envelope: a value plus the provenance that makes it
evidence rather than a guess.

measured.description:
Where the number came from: date, firmware, workload, and the
observed margins. Free text, for humans reading a warning.

value.description: The measured envelope value (unit is the field's, e.g. LEDs).

HwSoftLimits.description:
The soft-limit records a board manifest carries. All optional — a
manifest states only what has actually been measured.

totalLeds.description: Total LEDs across all wires this board×firmware has run clean at.

description:
Serializable board manifest file (authored as JSON).

This is the serializable form checked into the repo for board profiles. Use
[`HardwareManifestFile::to_manifest`] to validate and convert it into the
runtime [`HwManifest`].

soft_limits.description:
Measured soft-limit records (see [`HwSoftLimits`]): envelopes this
board×firmware has run clean at. Optional and additive — older
firmware parsing a manifest that carries them simply ignores the
field, which is what keeps this change format-compatible.

title: HardwareManifestFile
